protocol.scope: Use only the exact local-map kernels valid at every ring width; retain the eight-physical-tick job cap.
protocol.initial_phase: Eight jobs of transformation WW with inherited macro W, as in the parent model.
protocol.following_tasks: Alternate VV then WW for cycles in {1,2,4}; each block contains K jobs.
protocol.prices: Unchanged parent compile=8, replace=8, patch=min(8,1+2*Hamming), retain=0. Trace reserve is paid once at the beginning, not after every change.
protocol.capacity: One current four-letter macro and, for the revisable arm, its current editable trace. No free archive of earlier macros; returning to an earlier word pays the same management rule.

policies.replacement_oracle: Choose the cheapest complete macro sequence with all future task blocks known.
policies.revision_oracle: Same full-sequence optimization with revision fees and one prepaid trace reserve.
policies.replacement_reactive_lex: Minimize current-block management plus execution cost; break ties lexicographically; do not use subsequent tasks.
policies.revision_reactive_lex: Same reactive rule with revision fees.
policies.replacement_reactive_stay: Same reactive rule, but prefer the current macro when tied, then lexicographic order.
policies.revision_reactive_stay: Same reactive stay-on-tie rule with revision fees.

readouts: total cost sums and exact comparison counts
positive hindsight regret for each reactive policy
cost differences due to tie handling
revision gain relative to replacement under each matched information policy
costs and chosen macro paths for selected witnesses
strata: whether inherited compilation paid for itself before the change
protocol.witness_selection: First lexicographic (A,B,dispatch,trace,K,cycles,W,V) useful-inheritance example for reactive stay revision regret, reactive stay revision costing more than frozen, and any tie-rule cost difference. Also select the first primary-price four-cycle revision-oracle gain over replacement exceeding one unit. Preserve absence if no witness exists.
checks: dynamic programming matches direct enumeration of all 256 two-block macro paths for every pair, dispatch, W/V at K=4
every stored macro path replays its management and execution cost
hindsight oracle never costs more than its corresponding reactive policy
replacement oracle never costs more than frozen
zero-price physical execution has no library benefit
free-trace revision oracle weakly dominates replacement oracle
revision-oracle saving is bounded by 10*cycles minus trace reserve
limits: The oracle has more future information than the reactive benchmark; regret quantifies that information/planning gap, not a fair contest between learning algorithms.
The reactive benchmark deliberately does not use the repeating schedule; it does not learn that the task will return.
Current tasks and dynamics are fully known; search and task identification remain unpriced.
The trace stores the current construction only. No organizational survival or intrinsic agency is modeled.
Task, price, and cycle configurations share the same kernels and are not independent statistical replicates.
